31	**[Section 1: Purpose and Scope]{.underline}**
32	
33	This playbook provides negotiation guidance for Stratton Health Technologies, Inc. (\"Stratton Health\" or \"Controller\"), a Delaware corporation headquartered at 900 Lakeview Boulevard, Suite 1500, Austin, TX 78701, in connection with the Data Processing Agreement (the \"DPA\") to be entered into with CloudNest Infrastructure Services Ltd. (\"CloudNest\" or \"Processor\"), a corporation organized under the laws of England and Wales (Company No. 11482937), with its registered office at 45 Canary Wharf Tower, Level 22, London E14 5AB, United Kingdom.
34	
35	**Underlying Commercial Relationship.** On March 3, 2025, Stratton Health and CloudNest executed a Master Services Agreement (the \"MSA\") with a five-year term. The key financial terms of the MSA are as follows:
36	
37	> • Annual fees: \$18.6M per year
38	>
39	> • Total five-year contract value: \$93.0M
40	>
41	> • One-time setup fee: \$2.4M
42	>
43	> • Annual fee escalator: 3% for Years 3--5
44	
45	All playbook cap calculations and financial thresholds reference the base annual fee of \$18.6M and do not incorporate the 3% escalator unless otherwise stated.
46	
47	**Service and Infrastructure Context.** Under the MSA, CloudNest will host the StrattonCare telemedicine platform on dedicated infrastructure in CloudNest\'s London (United Kingdom) and Frankfurt (Germany) data centers. CloudNest is known to operate additional data centers in Dublin (Ireland), Mumbai (India), and São Paulo (Brazil). The DPA template restricts processing to the European Economic Area (\"EEA\"), the United Kingdom, and the United States only.
48	
49	**Data Processing Scope.** The DPA covers the following categories of Personal Data:
50	
51	1\. **Patient demographic data** --- name, date of birth, address, Social Security number / national identification number
52	
53	2\. **Clinical records** --- diagnoses, prescriptions, lab results
54	
55	3\. **Biometric identifiers** --- voice prints used for patient authentication
56	
57	4\. **Payment card data** --- within PCI DSS scope
58	
59	5\. **Behavioral/usage analytics** --- platform interaction and usage patterns
60	
61	The estimated initial data volume is 4.2 petabytes, projected to grow to approximately 8 petabytes over the five-year term. The estimated data subject population comprises approximately 2.3 million US patients, approximately 14,000 EU/UK patients (accessed through Stratton Health UK Ltd., a wholly owned subsidiary), and approximately 6,200 healthcare providers, for a total of approximately 2,320,200 data subjects.
62	
63	**Regulatory Framework.** The DPA must satisfy compliance requirements under the following regulatory regimes:
64	
65	1\. **HIPAA** --- CloudNest acts as a Business Associate under 45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164
66	
67	2\. **GDPR** --- CloudNest acts as Processor for EU/UK data subjects, with nexus through Stratton Health UK Ltd.
68	
69	3\. **UK Data Protection Act 2018** --- as applied through the UK GDPR
70	
71	4\. **CCPA/CPRA** --- California Consumer Privacy Act, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act
72	
73	5\. **Texas Data Privacy and Security Act (TDPSA)**
74	
75	6\. **PCI DSS v4.0** --- for payment card data handling
76	
77	**Known Sub-Processor.** CloudNest utilizes Peregrine Data Analytics Pvt. Ltd. (\"Peregrine\"), an Indian private limited company located at 7th Floor, Bandra-Kurla Tech Park, Bandra East, Mumbai 400051, India, for log analytics and performance monitoring. India does not hold an EU adequacy decision. Peregrine\'s activities on a telemedicine platform likely involve exposure to data that may constitute Personal Data or PHI.
78	
79	**Procedural Status.** The DPA template was sent by Whitfield & Crane LLP to Barrington Reeves LLP (outside counsel to CloudNest, London, UK) on March 10, 2025. This playbook anticipates CloudNest\'s markup and covers 18 negotiation topics with tiered positions for each.
80	
81	**[Section 2: Classification Framework]{.underline}**
82	
83	**[2.1 Three-Tier Classification System]{.underline}**
84	
85	This playbook employs a three-tier classification system for evaluating counterparty positions proposed by CloudNest during DPA negotiations. Each counterparty deviation from Stratton Health\'s template language is classified into one of the following categories:
86	
87	**Green (Acceptable).** Counterparty positions that may be accepted without escalation. Green positions represent commercially reasonable modifications that do not materially increase legal, regulatory, or commercial risk to Stratton Health. The handling attorney (David Ngata, Associate, Whitfield & Crane LLP) may accept Green positions in the ordinary course of negotiation without further internal approval. Green acceptances must be documented in the negotiation log but do not require additional sign-off.
88	
89	**Yellow (Escalate).** Counterparty positions that require escalation to and written sign-off from the Chief Privacy Officer (Anisha Ramachandran) or General Counsel (Jonathan Pryce-Whitaker) before acceptance. Yellow positions represent moderate risk that may be acceptable with appropriate mitigating conditions, compensating controls, or business justification. The handling attorney must prepare a brief written analysis of the deviation, the associated risk, and a recommended response before forwarding the matter for decision. Yellow positions may not be accepted by the handling attorney without explicit written approval from the CPO or GC.
90	
91	**Red (Reject).** Counterparty positions that must be rejected. Stratton Health\'s original template language must be restored. Red positions represent unacceptable legal, regulatory, or commercial risk. The default response to any Red position is rejection with restoration of the Stratton Health template language. Any deviation from a Red rejection requires CEO-level approval (Dr. Miriam Osei-Kwame) and a written risk acceptance memorandum co-signed by the General Counsel and Chief Privacy Officer. Red overrides should be treated as exceptional and are expected to be rare.
92	
93	**[2.2 Escalation Matrix]{.underline}**
94	
95	  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
96	  **Classification**   **Initial Review**             **Decision Authority**                                          **Required Action**
97	  -------------------- ------------------------------ --------------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
98	  **Green**            David Ngata (Associate, W&C)   David Ngata                                                     Accept; document in negotiation log
99	
100	  **Yellow**           David Ngata (Associate, W&C)   Anisha Ramachandran (CPO) and/or Jonathan Pryce-Whitaker (GC)   Accept/reject with conditions; written sign-off required
101	
102	  **Red**              David Ngata (Associate, W&C)   Jonathan Pryce-Whitaker (GC) → reject                           Reject; restore template language. Override requires CEO approval + written risk acceptance memo
103	  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
104	
105	**[2.3 Governing Rules]{.underline}**
106	
107	**Compound Classification.** Where a single counterparty change triggers both a Yellow and a Red sub-issue, the overall classification is **Red**. The most restrictive classification always governs.
108	
109	**Unaddressed Positions.** Any counterparty positions not explicitly addressed in the 18 topics set forth in this playbook should be treated as **Yellow** and escalated to the CPO for assessment. The handling attorney should provide a brief analysis of the legal and commercial implications of the unaddressed change to facilitate timely decision-making.
110	
111	**[Section 3: Negotiation Topic Positions]{.underline}**
112	
113	**[Topic 1: Sub-Processing (DPA Section 7)]{.underline}**
114	
115	**Stratton Health Template Position.** Prior specific written consent is required for each sub-processor, consistent with GDPR Art. 28(2). Controller must be notified at least 30 days in advance of any proposed new sub-processor or replacement. Controller has the right to object to any proposed sub-processor within 15 days of receiving notice. If the objection is not resolved to Controller\'s satisfaction within 15 days of the objection, Controller has the right to terminate the DPA and MSA without penalty.
116	
117	**Green.** Minor editorial changes that do not alter the consent mechanism, notice period, or objection/termination right. Addition of reasonable detail regarding evaluation criteria for sub-processors (e.g., security posture, geographic location, certifications) is acceptable and may strengthen the clause.
118	
119	**Yellow.** Reduction of the advance notice period from 30 days to no fewer than 20 days, provided the objection and termination rights remain intact. Addition of a requirement that Controller\'s objection must be on \"reasonable grounds\" --- acceptable only with CPO sign-off and only if \"reasonable grounds\" is defined to include data protection, security, and jurisdictional concerns.
120	
121	**Red.** Any change from \"prior specific written consent\" to \"general written authorization\" or similar general consent model. Any reduction of the notice period below 20 days. Any removal or material weakening of the right to object. Any removal or conditioning of the termination right following an unresolved objection. **All three elements** --- consent type, notice period, and objection/termination right --- must be preserved. Failure to preserve any one of these three elements renders the deviation Red.
122	
123	**Rationale.** GDPR Art. 28(2) permits either specific or general authorization, but specific consent is the more protective standard. Given CloudNest\'s known use of Peregrine Data Analytics Pvt. Ltd. in Mumbai, India --- a jurisdiction without an EU adequacy decision --- maintaining specific consent control is essential. HIPAA also requires that business associates ensure any subcontractor handling PHI agrees to equivalent restrictions (45 CFR § 164.504(e)(2)(ii)(D)), making sub-processor control a dual-regime compliance issue. The termination right provides Controller with an exit ramp if Processor proposes a sub-processor that creates unacceptable risk.
124	
125	**[Topic 2: Data Breach Notification (DPA Section 8)]{.underline}**
126	
127	**Stratton Health Template Position.** Processor must notify Controller within **24 hours** of becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach. Notification must include four enumerated content elements: (1) the nature of the breach, including the categories of data affected; (2) the categories and approximate number of data subjects affected; (3) the likely consequences of the breach; and (4) the measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its effects.
128	
129	**Green.** Minor clarifications to the definition of \"becoming aware\" (e.g., \"when a senior officer of the Processor with responsibility for data protection first becomes aware\") are acceptable provided they do not change the substantive trigger or introduce a delay mechanism. Addition of a requirement for Controller to provide a secure communication channel for notifications is acceptable and prudent.
130	
131	**Yellow.** Extension of the notification window from 24 hours up to a maximum of **36 hours**. Removal of one (but not more than one) of the four content elements, provided the remaining three include: the nature of the breach, the approximate number of data subjects, and the measures taken or proposed. Addition of a \"reasonable efforts\" qualifier to content completeness (i.e., Processor provides information to the extent known at the time and supplements as further details become available) is acceptable as Yellow.
132	
133	**Red.** Extension of the notification window **beyond 36 hours**. Any change to the notification trigger from \"becoming aware\" to a standard that allows delay --- such as \"upon confirmation,\" \"upon determination,\" \"upon concluding its investigation,\" or similar language that introduces a subjective assessment gate between awareness and notification. Removal of two or more of the four required content elements. Any provision that conditions notification on materiality thresholds or excludes categories of breaches from the notification requirement.
134	
135	**Rationale.** HIPAA requires notification to covered entities without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 days (45 CFR § 164.410), but Stratton Health\'s contractual standard is intentionally more aggressive to allow Stratton Health to meet its own downstream notification obligations. GDPR Art. 33(2) requires processor notification \"without undue delay.\" The 24-hour standard reflects the operational reality that Stratton Health must assess, investigate, and potentially notify supervisory authorities within 72 hours under GDPR. The trigger language change (from \"becoming aware\" to \"confirming\") is specifically identified as Red because it introduces a subjective determination that could delay notification indefinitely under the guise of ongoing investigation.
136	
137	**[Topic 3: Audit Rights (DPA Section 9)]{.underline}**
138	
139	**Stratton Health Template Position.** Controller has unlimited audit rights, including on-site inspections of Processor\'s facilities and systems, upon **15 business days\'** written notice, at Controller\'s cost. Processor may not substitute third-party audit reports (e.g., SOC 2, ISO 27001) for on-site audit rights. Processor must cooperate fully and provide access to relevant personnel, systems, records, and data centers.
140	
141	**Green.** Addition of reasonable confidentiality protections for audit findings. Requirement that auditors execute NDAs. Limitation of routine audits to once per 12-month period, provided Controller retains the right to additional audits following a breach, regulatory investigation, or material security incident. Provision that Controller shall use reasonable efforts to minimize disruption to Processor\'s operations during audits.
142	
143	**Yellow.** Extension of the notice period from 15 business days to no more than **20 business days**. Provision that Controller may review third-party audit reports (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001) as a first step, but retains the right to conduct on-site audits if the reports are insufficient, raise concerns, or do not cover the relevant systems and data centers. Limitation of routine audits to once per 12-month period with unlimited audit rights triggered by a breach, complaint, or regulatory inquiry.
144	
145	**Red.** Elimination of on-site audit rights entirely, or restricting on-site audits to post-breach scenarios only. Substitution of third-party audit reports as the sole audit mechanism with no on-site access. Extension of the notice period beyond 20 business days. Any requirement that Controller bear Processor\'s costs in facilitating an audit (as opposed to Controller\'s own audit costs). Any provision granting Processor the right to refuse or delay an audit.
146	
147	**Rationale.** GDPR Art. 28(3)(h) requires that the processor \"makes available to the controller all information necessary to demonstrate compliance\" and \"allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by the controller.\" Reliance on third-party reports alone does not satisfy this obligation. HIPAA also requires business associates to make practices, books, and records available to HHS (45 CFR § 164.504(e)(2)(ii)(H)). SOC 2 and ISO 27001 reports from Thornfield Audit Partners LLP (CloudNest\'s auditor) are valuable supplementary assurance but cannot substitute for Controller\'s direct inspection rights over a processor handling PHI and biometric data for over 2.3 million patients.
148	
149	**[Topic 4: Data Localization and International Transfers (DPA Section 10)]{.underline}**
150	
151	**Stratton Health Template Position.** All processing of Personal Data must occur within the **EEA, UK, or United States**. No transfers to any country outside these jurisdictions unless: (a) the destination country has been granted an adequacy decision by the European Commission or the UK Secretary of State, or (b) appropriate safeguards are in place under GDPR Art. 46 (e.g., Standard Contractual Clauses, binding corporate rules) and such safeguards have been approved in writing by Controller in advance.
152	
153	**Green.** Addition of explicit references to specific adequacy decisions (e.g., EU-US Data Privacy Framework). Clarification of the approval process for transfer mechanisms (e.g., timelines for Controller review of proposed SCCs).
154	
155	**Yellow.** Expansion to include a specific named country that has a current EU adequacy decision (e.g., Canada, Japan, South Korea), provided Processor demonstrates a legitimate processing need. Addition of a transfer impact assessment requirement prior to any transfer under SCCs.
156	
157	**Red.** Addition of processing locations in countries without an EU adequacy decision (e.g., India, Brazil) without referencing an approved transfer mechanism (SCCs, BCRs, or equivalent). Any provision that permits transfers based solely on Processor\'s internal assessment of adequacy. Any removal of the requirement for Controller\'s prior written approval of transfer safeguards. Processing in any non-adequate country without approved Article 46 safeguards is a firm Red.

159	**Rationale.** CloudNest operates data centers in Mumbai (India) and São Paulo (Brazil), neither of which has an EU adequacy decision. Peregrine Data Analytics Pvt. Ltd. (Mumbai) processes log data and performance monitoring data. If any Personal Data --- including metadata that could identify individuals, such as IP addresses linked to patient sessions or error logs containing clinical data identifiers --- is routed to Peregrine, this constitutes an international transfer requiring safeguards under GDPR Chapter V. Under HIPAA, any sub-processor handling PHI must be covered by a Business Associate Agreement chain (45 CFR § 164.504(e)(2)(ii)(D)), and processing of PHI in jurisdictions outside US regulatory reach creates enforcement and compliance risks that cannot be mitigated by contractual provisions alone.

235	**[Topic 11: Processor Use of Personal Data / Anonymization (DPA Section 14)]{.underline}**
236	
237	**Stratton Health Template Position.** Processor shall process Personal Data solely on behalf of and in accordance with Controller\'s documented instructions. Processor shall not anonymize, aggregate, de-identify, or otherwise derive any data products from Personal Data for Processor\'s own purposes, including but not limited to service improvement, benchmarking, research, marketing, or sale to third parties. Any anonymization or de-identification must be performed only at Controller\'s written direction and must comply with applicable standards, including HIPAA de-identification requirements under 45 CFR § 164.514(b) --- either the **Safe Harbor method** (18 identifiers removed per § 164.514(b)(2)) or the **Expert Determination method** (§ 164.514(b)(1)).
238	
239	**Green.** Clarification that Processor may use aggregated, fully de-identified data (compliant with HIPAA Safe Harbor or Expert Determination standards) for capacity planning purposes only, with Controller\'s prior written consent and with no retention beyond the period necessary for such planning.
240	
241	**Yellow.** Processor request to use de-identified or anonymized data for internal service improvement, provided **all six** of the following conditions are met: (a) de-identification meets HIPAA Safe Harbor or Expert Determination standards; (b) anonymization meets GDPR Recital 26 standard (reasonably impossible to re-identify); (c) Controller\'s prior written consent is obtained for each use case; (d) retention period is limited to 12 months; (e) no transfer to third parties; and (f) express prohibition on re-identification attempts.
242	
243	**Red.** Any provision granting Processor the right to anonymize, aggregate, or de-identify Personal Data **without Controller\'s prior written consent**. Any provision without explicit compliance with HIPAA de-identification standards. Any provision without a retention limit. Any provision without a prohibition on re-identification. Any provision permitting use for \"benchmarking,\" \"research,\" or commercial purposes beyond internal service improvement. Any provision that does not distinguish between HIPAA de-identification and GDPR anonymization standards. Any provision effectively allowing Processor to derive commercial value from patient health data.
244	
245	**Rationale.** HIPAA\'s minimum necessary standard limits use and disclosure of PHI. GDPR\'s purpose limitation principle (Art. 5(1)(b)) restricts processing to specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes. \"Anonymized\" data that does not meet HIPAA\'s specific de-identification methodology remains PHI and is subject to all HIPAA restrictions. Under GDPR, true anonymization (Recital 26) removes data from GDPR scope, but the threshold is high and a processor\'s self-described \"anonymization\" may not meet either standard. This concern is particularly acute where the underlying data includes clinical records, biometric identifiers, and behavioral analytics --- categories with high re-identification risk.

The security measures must meet or exceed: (a) HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C), (b) GDPR Art. 32, (c) PCI DSS v4.0 (for payment card data), and (d) industry standards for cloud infrastructure providers handling sensitive health data.

251	**Green.** Addition of detail to Annex 2 security measures (e.g., specifying encryption algorithms, key management procedures, access control protocols). Clarification that security measures will be reviewed and updated at least annually to reflect evolving threats.

253	**Yellow.** Processor request to substitute or update specific security measures in Annex 2 with equivalent or superior measures, subject to Controller\'s prior written approval. This is expected and encouraged as security evolves.

255	**Red.** Any change from absolute compliance to a **\"commercially reasonable efforts,\"** **\"best efforts,\"** or similar standard. Any safe harbor provision limiting accountability for security failures based on adherence to a generalized standard rather than the specific Annex 2 measures. 369	**Step 1 --- Initial Review.** Upon receipt of the counterparty markup from Barrington Reeves LLP, David Ngata (Associate, Whitfield & Crane LLP) will review each deviation against this playbook and classify each as Green, Yellow, or Red. 372	
373	**Step 3 --- Yellow Deviations.** For each Yellow deviation, David Ngata prepares a summary memorandum that includes: (a) the specific counterparty language; (b) the corresponding playbook topic and classification; (c) the legal and commercial risk analysis; and (d) a recommended response (accept, accept with conditions, or counter-propose). This report is forwarded to Jonathan Pryce-Whitaker (GC) for review. The GC reviews within 2 business days and provides direction. The default response is **rejection and restoration of template language**. 114	**3.1** Controller shall ensure that its instructions to Processor for the Processing of Personal Data comply with Applicable Data Protection Laws. Controller shall be responsible for determining the lawfulness of the Processing instructions it provides to Processor under this Agreement.
115	
116	**3.2** Controller shall ensure that it has a lawful basis for the Processing of Personal Data under Article 6 of the EU GDPR and the UK GDPR (and, where applicable, a condition for processing special categories of personal data under Article 9 of the EU GDPR and the UK GDPR), and that all necessary consents, authorizations, and notices have been obtained or provided to Data Subjects in connection with the Processing contemplated by this Agreement.
117	
118	**3.3** Controller shall notify Processor promptly, and in any event within fifteen (15) business days, of any changes to the Processing activities described in Annex 1, including changes to the categories of Personal Data, categories of Data Subjects, or the purposes of Processing.
119	
120	**3.4** Controller shall be responsible for the accuracy, quality, and legality of Personal Data provided to Processor and for the means by which Controller acquired such Personal Data.
121	
122	**3.5** Controller shall designate a point of contact for data protection matters arising under this Agreement. As of the Effective Date, Controller\'s point of contact is **Anisha Ramachandran, Chief Privacy Officer, Stratton Health Technologies, Inc.**, who may be reached at the contact details set out in Section 21 (Notices).
123	
124	**[SECTION 4: PROCESSOR\'S OBLIGATIONS]{.underline}**
125	
126	**4.1** Processor shall Process Personal Data only on documented instructions from Controller, including with regard to transfers of Personal Data to a third country or an international organization, unless Processor is required to Process Personal Data by Union or Member State law to which Processor is subject or by other applicable law; in such a case, Processor shall inform Controller of that legal requirement before Processing commences, unless the applicable law prohibits such notification on important grounds of public interest.
127	
128	**4.2** Processor shall ensure that all persons authorized to Process Personal Data, including Processor\'s employees, agents, and contractors, have committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality before being granted access to Personal Data. Processor shall maintain records of all such confidentiality undertakings and shall make such records available to Controller upon request.
129	
130	**4.3** Processor shall implement and maintain, at its own cost, the technical and organizational security measures described in Section 8 and Annex 2 (Technical and Organizational Security Measures) throughout the Term of this Agreement. Processor shall ensure that such measures provide a level of security appropriate to the risks presented by the Processing, taking into account the state of the art, the costs of implementation, and the nature, scope, context, and purposes of the Processing, as well as the sensitivity of the Personal Data Processed (including PHI, Biometric Data, and payment card data).
131	
132	**4.4** Processor shall comply with the conditions for engaging Sub-Processors set out in Section 7 of this Agreement.
133	
134	**4.5** Processor shall assist Controller in responding to Data Subject Requests in accordance with Section 9 of this Agreement.
135	
136	**4.6** Processor shall assist Controller in ensuring compliance with the obligations pursuant to Articles 32 through 36 of the EU GDPR and the UK GDPR (security of processing, notification of personal data breaches, communication of personal data breaches to data subjects, data protection impact assessments, and prior consultation with supervisory authorities) and the HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C), taking into account the nature of the Processing and the information available to Processor.
137	
138	**4.7** Processor shall, at the choice of Controller, delete or return all Personal Data upon termination of the Services in accordance with Section 13 (Data Return and Deletion) of this Agreement.
139	
140	**4.8** Processor shall make available to Controller all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with the obligations laid down in this Agreement and in Article 28 of the EU GDPR and the UK GDPR, and shall allow for and contribute to audits and inspections conducted by Controller or an auditor mandated by Controller, in accordance with Section 10 (Audit Rights) of this Agreement.
141	
142	**4.9** Processor shall immediately inform Controller if, in Processor\'s opinion, an instruction from Controller infringes Applicable Data Protection Laws. Processor shall not be required to carry out the instruction pending Controller\'s response, but shall not unreasonably delay notification to Controller.
143	
144	**4.10** Processor shall designate a Data Protection Officer in accordance with Article 37 of the EU GDPR and the UK GDPR (to the extent required) and shall ensure that a qualified individual is responsible for overseeing Processor\'s compliance with this Agreement. As of the Effective Date, Processor\'s Data Protection Officer is **Dr. Henrik Lindqvist, CloudNest Infrastructure Services Ltd.**, who may be reached at the contact details set out in Section 21 (Notices).
145	
146	**[SECTION 5: DATA LOCALIZATION AND INTERNATIONAL TRANSFERS]{.underline}**
147	
148	**5.1 Permitted Processing Locations**
149	
150	All Processing of Personal Data under this Agreement shall take place exclusively within the European Economic Area (EEA), the United Kingdom, or the United States of America (collectively, the **\"Permitted Processing Locations\"**). As of the Effective Date, Processor is authorized to Process Personal Data at the following facilities only:
151	
152	> \(a\) **London, United Kingdom** --- CloudNest UK Data Center, Docklands Campus; and
153	>
154	> \(b\) **Frankfurt, Germany** --- CloudNest EU Data Center, Frankfurt-Rödelheim Campus.
155	
156	No other processing locations are authorized as of the Effective Date. The addition of any processing location, whether within or outside the Permitted Processing Locations, shall require the prior written consent of Controller in accordance with the procedures set out in this Section 5 and, where a new Sub-Processor is involved, in accordance with Section 7.
157	
158	**5.2 Prohibition on Unauthorized Transfers**
159	
160	Processor shall not transfer, access, store, or otherwise Process Personal Data in any country outside the Permitted Processing Locations described in Section 5.1 without the prior written consent of Controller and without ensuring that one or more of the following transfer mechanisms is in place for each such transfer:
161	
162	> \(a\) an adequacy decision by the European Commission pursuant to Article 45 of the EU GDPR, or by the UK Secretary of State pursuant to section 17A of the UK Data Protection Act 2018, as applicable;
163	>
164	> \(b\) appropriate safeguards under Article 46 of the EU GDPR or section 17C of the UK Data Protection Act 2018, including Standard Contractual Clauses approved by the European Commission or the UK International Data Transfer Agreement or UK Addendum to the EU SCCs, as applicable;
165	>
166	> \(c\) binding corporate rules approved by a competent Supervisory Authority under Article 47 of the EU GDPR; or
167	>
168	> \(d\) another legally recognized transfer mechanism under Applicable Data Protection Laws, approved by Controller in writing in advance of the transfer.
169	
170	For the avoidance of doubt, Processor shall not rely on any derogation under Article 49 of the EU GDPR for recurring or systematic transfers of Personal Data.
171	
172	**5.3 Transfer Impact Assessments**
173	
174	Where a transfer mechanism under Section 5.2(b) or (c) is relied upon, Processor shall, prior to commencing any transfer, conduct a transfer impact assessment evaluating whether the laws and practices of the destination country provide an essentially equivalent level of protection to that guaranteed within the EEA or the United Kingdom, taking into account the guidance of the European Data Protection Board (EDPB Recommendations 01/2020) and the UK Information Commissioner\'s Office. Processor shall provide the results of each transfer impact assessment to Controller for review and approval prior to commencing the transfer. Controller shall have the right to reject or impose conditions on any proposed transfer based on the results of the transfer impact assessment.
175	
176	**5.4 Government Access Requests**
177	
178	Where Personal Data is Processed in a location outside the EEA or United Kingdom, Processor shall promptly notify Controller of any legally binding request for disclosure of Personal Data by a law enforcement authority or government body, unless such notification is prohibited by applicable law. Processor shall use all reasonable legal mechanisms to challenge such requests where there are reasonable grounds to consider the request unlawful.
179	
180	**[SECTION 6: CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**
181	
182	**6.1** Processor shall ensure that access to Personal Data is limited strictly to those personnel who require access in order to perform the Services and who are bound by appropriate written confidentiality obligations, whether by contract, professional duty, or statutory obligation, that are no less protective than the confidentiality obligations set out in this Agreement and the MSA.
183	
184	**6.2** Processor shall ensure that any natural person acting under Processor\'s authority who has access to Personal Data shall not Process such data except on documented instructions from Controller, unless required to do so by applicable law to which that person is subject.
185	
186	**6.3** Processor shall maintain and enforce policies and procedures to ensure that Personal Data is not disclosed to unauthorized persons, whether employees of Processor or third parties, and shall take appropriate disciplinary action against any personnel who access or disclose Personal Data in violation of this Agreement.
187	
188	**6.4** The confidentiality obligations in this Section 6 are in addition to (and not in substitution for) any confidentiality obligations in the MSA and shall survive the termination or expiry of this Agreement indefinitely.
189	
190	**[SECTION 7: SUB-PROCESSING]{.underline}**
191	
192	**7.1 Prior Specific Written Consent**
193	
194	Processor shall not engage any Sub-Processor to carry out any Processing activities on behalf of Controller without obtaining the **prior specific written consent** of Controller for each proposed Sub-Processor. Controller\'s consent must be obtained separately for each proposed Sub-Processor before such Sub-Processor commences any Processing of Personal Data. For the avoidance of doubt, general written authorization is not sufficient; each Sub-Processor engagement requires individual, specific written approval from Controller.
195	
196	**7.2 Advance Notice of New Sub-Processors**
197	
198	Processor shall provide Controller with at least **thirty (30) calendar days\'** advance written notice of any intended engagement of a new Sub-Processor or replacement of an existing Sub-Processor. Such notice shall include the following information:
199	
200	> \(a\) the full legal name and registered address of the proposed Sub-Processor;
201	>
202	> \(b\) the location(s) from which the Sub-Processor will Process Personal Data, including the specific country and city of each data center or facility to be used;
203	>
204	> \(c\) a detailed description of the nature and scope of the Processing activities to be performed by the Sub-Processor;
205	>
206	> \(d\) the technical and organizational security measures the Sub-Processor will implement to protect Personal Data, including a summary of relevant certifications and audit reports; and
207	>
208	> \(e\) a copy of the proposed sub-processing agreement or a detailed summary of its material terms, including data protection provisions.
209	
210	**7.3 Right to Object**
211	
212	Controller shall have the right to object to the appointment of any proposed Sub-Processor on reasonable data protection grounds. If Controller notifies Processor of such an objection in writing within the thirty (30) day notice period specified in Section 7.2, the Parties shall discuss the objection in good faith with a view to achieving a commercially reasonable resolution, which may include Processor proposing an alternative Sub-Processor or implementing additional safeguards. If the Parties are unable to resolve the objection within **fifteen (15) calendar days** of Controller\'s written objection, Controller shall have the right to terminate this Agreement and the affected portions of the MSA immediately upon written notice, without incurring any penalty, early termination fee, or other charge, and Processor shall comply with its obligations under Section 13 (Data Return and Deletion).
213	
214	**7.4 Sub-Processor Obligations**
215	
216	Processor shall impose on each Sub-Processor, by way of a written agreement, data protection obligations that are no less protective than those imposed on Processor under this Agreement. Where a Sub-Processor will Process PHI, the sub-processing agreement must also satisfy the requirements of a Business Associate subcontractor agreement under 45 CFR § 164.502(e)(1)(ii) and § 164.504(e)(2)(ii)(D), and must contain all provisions required by the HIPAA Privacy Rule and HIPAA Security Rule for such agreements.
217	
218	**7.5 Liability for Sub-Processors**
219	
220	Processor shall remain fully liable to Controller for the performance of each Sub-Processor\'s obligations under the applicable sub-processing agreement. Any act or omission of a Sub-Processor that would constitute a breach of this Agreement if committed by Processor shall be deemed a breach by Processor under this Agreement. Processor shall not be relieved of any obligation under this Agreement by reason of having delegated the performance of such obligation to a Sub-Processor.

223	
224	The Sub-Processors approved by Controller as of the Effective Date are listed in Annex 3 (Approved Sub-Processors). **As of the Effective Date, no Sub-Processors have been approved by Controller.** Annex 3 shall be updated from time to time by the mutual written agreement of the Parties to reflect any Sub-Processors subsequently approved by Controller in accordance with this Section 7.

227	
228	**8.1 Technical and Organizational Measures**
229	
230	Processor **shall** implement and maintain the technical and organizational security measures set out in Annex 2 (Technical and Organizational Security Measures) throughout the Term of this Agreement. These measures shall include, at a minimum, measures designed to:
231	
232	> \(a\) ensure the ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability, and resilience of Processing systems and services;
233	>
234	> \(b\) restore the availability of and access to Personal Data in a timely manner in the event of a physical or technical incident;
235	>
236	> \(c\) regularly test, assess, and evaluate the effectiveness of technical and organizational measures for ensuring the security of Processing; and
237	>
238	> \(d\) pseudonymize and encrypt Personal Data where appropriate, having regard to the state of the art and the nature of the Processing.
239	
240	The measures set out in Annex 2 represent the minimum required standards; Processor may implement additional measures, but shall not reduce the level of protection below that described in Annex 2 without the prior written consent of Controller.
241	
242	**8.2 Security Certifications**
243	
244	Processor shall obtain and maintain current the following certifications throughout the entire Term of this Agreement:
245	
246	> \(a\) **ISO/IEC 27001:2022** --- Information Security Management Systems;
247	>
248	> \(b\) **SOC 2 Type II** --- Trust Services Criteria (Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy); and
249	>
250	> \(c\) **HITRUST CSF Certification** (or its successor standard), appropriate to the scope of the Services and the types of Personal Data Processed.
251	
252	Processor shall provide Controller with copies of all current certification reports, including detailed audit findings and any corrective action plans, **annually**, and in any event within thirty (30) calendar days of the issuance of each report. Processor shall promptly notify Controller of any lapse, suspension, revocation, or material qualification of any such certification, and any such lapse, suspension, or revocation shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement.
253	
254	**8.3 HIPAA Security Rule Compliance**
255	
256	Without limiting the generality of Section 8.1, Processor shall implement administrative safeguards, physical safeguards, and technical safeguards that reasonably and appropriately protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of ePHI, as required by the HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C). Processor shall comply with 45 CFR § 164.308 (administrative safeguards), § 164.310 (physical safeguards), § 164.312 (technical safeguards), and § 164.316 (policies and procedures and documentation requirements). Processor shall conduct a risk analysis in accordance with 45 CFR § 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A) and implement measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level.
257	
258	**8.4 PCI DSS Compliance**
259	
260	To the extent that Processor Processes, stores, or transmits payment card data in connection with the Services, Processor shall comply with PCI DSS v4.0 and shall provide Controller with evidence of such compliance (including an Attestation of Compliance or Report on Compliance issued by a Qualified Security Assessor) annually, and in any event within thirty (30) calendar days of issuance. Processor shall promptly notify Controller of any non-compliance with PCI DSS requirements.
261	
262	**8.5 No Reduction in Security**
263	
264	Processor shall not reduce the overall level of security protection provided to Personal Data during the Term of this Agreement without the prior written consent of Controller. Any proposed change to the security measures described in Annex 2 that would result in a reduction of the level of protection shall be submitted to Controller for review and approval at least sixty (60) calendar days in advance. Controller shall have the right to reject any such change.
265	
266	**[SECTION 9: DATA SUBJECT RIGHTS]{.underline}**
267	
268	**9.1 Assistance with Data Subject Requests**
269	
270	Processor shall, taking into account the nature of the Processing, assist Controller by implementing appropriate technical and organizational measures, insofar as this is possible, in fulfilling Controller\'s obligation to respond to Data Subject Requests exercised under Applicable Data Protection Laws, including rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, data portability, and objection. Processor shall promptly, and in any event within two (2) business days, notify Controller upon receiving a Data Subject Request directly and shall not respond to any such request without Controller\'s prior written authorization, except to confirm receipt of the request and to direct the Data Subject to Controller.
271	
272	**9.2 Response Timeline**
273	
274	Upon receiving a forwarded Data Subject Request from Controller, or upon receiving Controller\'s instructions regarding a Data Subject Request received directly by Processor, Processor shall implement the technical actions required to fulfill the request within **five (5) business days** of receipt of such instructions. Where the complexity of a request requires additional time, Processor shall notify Controller within two (2) business days and shall use best efforts to complete the required actions within ten (10) business days.
275	
276	**9.3 No Fee for Assistance**
277	
278	Processor shall not charge Controller any additional fee, cost, or expense for providing assistance with Data Subject Requests under this Section 9. The costs of fulfilling Data Subject Requests are included in the fees payable under the MSA, regardless of the volume or frequency of such requests. Processor acknowledges that the ability to respond to Data Subject Requests in a timely manner is a critical component of the Services.
279	
280	**[SECTION 10: AUDIT RIGHTS]{.underline}**
281	
282	**10.1 Right to Audit**
283	
284	Controller shall have the right, at its own cost (except as otherwise provided in Section 10.5), to conduct audits and inspections of Processor\'s Processing activities, systems, facilities, and records relevant to the Processing of Personal Data under this Agreement. Audits may include **on-site inspections** of Processor\'s data centers, offices, and any other premises where Personal Data is Processed, stored, accessed, or from which Personal Data may be accessed. Audits may be conducted by Controller\'s internal audit team, by Controller\'s Chief Privacy Officer or designee, or by a qualified independent third-party auditor selected and mandated by Controller.
285	
286	**10.2 Scope and Frequency**
287	
288	Controller may exercise its audit rights under this Section 10 at reasonable intervals, and in any event no less than **once per calendar year**. Audits shall be conducted during Processor\'s normal business hours and shall be planned and executed in a manner that does not unreasonably interfere with Processor\'s day-to-day operations. The scope of each audit may include, without limitation: (a) review of Processor\'s policies, procedures, and records relating to data protection and information security; (b) inspection of technical infrastructure, including servers, storage systems, network configurations, and access control mechanisms; (c) interviews with Processor\'s personnel responsible for data protection and security; (d) review of Sub-Processor agreements and compliance documentation; and (e) verification of compliance with the technical and organizational measures described in Annex 2.
289	
290	**10.3 Notice.** Controller shall provide Processor with at least **fifteen (15) business days\'** prior written notice of an intended audit, specifying the proposed scope, duration, and personnel involved. Notwithstanding the foregoing, **no prior notice shall be required** where Controller has reasonable grounds to believe that: (a) a Personal Data Breach has occurred or is occurring; (b) Processor is in material breach of this Agreement; or (c) a Supervisory Authority or regulatory body has required or requested an audit of Processor\'s Processing activities. In such circumstances, Controller may conduct an audit immediately upon arrival at Processor\'s premises, and Processor shall provide full cooperation without delay.
291	
292	**10.4 Third-Party Audit Reports**
293	
294	Processor shall make available to Controller, promptly upon request and in any event within ten (10) business days of the request, copies of relevant third-party audit and certification reports, including SOC 2 Type II reports prepared by Thornfield Audit Partners LLP, ISO 27001 certification reports, HITRUST CSF certification reports, and any other reports relevant to the security of Personal Data. **Such third-party reports shall supplement, but shall not substitute for, Controller\'s right to conduct its own audits and on-site inspections under this Section 10.** The availability of third-party reports shall not limit, restrict, or otherwise condition Controller\'s independent audit rights in any manner.
295	
296	**10.5 Audit Cooperation**
297	
298	Processor shall cooperate fully and in good faith with Controller\'s audits, including by providing timely access to relevant records, systems, facilities, and personnel, and by responding promptly and completely to all reasonable requests for information. Processor shall promptly remediate any deficiencies, non-conformities, or vulnerabilities identified during an audit, at Processor\'s sole cost and expense, and shall provide Controller with evidence of remediation within thirty (30) calendar days of the audit findings, or such shorter period as the severity of the deficiency may require.
299	
300	**10.6 Regulatory Audits**
301	
302	Processor shall cooperate with and permit audits, inspections, and investigations by any Supervisory Authority or regulatory body with jurisdiction over Controller or Processor, including the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Office for Civil Rights (OCR), the UK Information Commissioner\'s Office (ICO), and any EU data protection authority. Processor shall promptly notify Controller of any audit, inspection, or investigation by a Supervisory Authority that relates to or could reasonably affect the Processing of Personal Data under this Agreement.

305

307	
308	Processor shall notify Controller of any Personal Data Breach **within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware** of such breach. For the purposes of this Section 11, Processor shall be deemed to have become \"aware\" of a Personal Data Breach when any employee, officer, agent, or Sub-Processor of Processor has a reasonable basis to believe that a Personal Data Breach has occurred, regardless of whether such breach has been confirmed through a formal investigation. Processor shall promptly notify Controller of any audit, inspection, or investigation by a Supervisory Authority that relates to or could reasonably affect the Processing of Personal Data under this Agreement.

**[SECTION 11: PERSONAL DATA BREACH NOTIFICATION]{.underline}**

**11.1 Notification to Controller**

Processor shall notify Controller of any Personal Data Breach **within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware** of such breach. For the purposes of this Section 11, Processor shall be deemed to have become \"aware\" of a Personal Data Breach when any employee, officer, agent, or Sub-Processor of Processor has a reasonable basis to believe that a Personal Data Breach has occurred, regardless of whether such breach has been confirmed through a formal investigation. Notification shall be made to Controller\'s Chief Privacy Officer (Anisha Ramachandran) and General Counsel (Jonathan Pryce-Whitaker) via both email and telephone, using the contact details set out in Section 21 (Notices). An initial notification may be made orally (by telephone) and shall be confirmed in writing (by email) within the twenty-four (24) hour period.

**11.2 Content of Notification**

The notification under Section 11.1 shall include, to the extent known at the time of notification, the following information (with updates to follow promptly as further information becomes available during the course of the investigation):

> \(a\) a description of the **nature of the Personal Data Breach**, including the categories of Personal Data and the categories of Processing systems affected;
>
> \(b\) the **categories and approximate number of Data Subjects** affected by the breach;
>
> \(c\) a description of the **likely consequences** of the Personal Data Breach, including an assessment of the potential harm to affected Data Subjects; and
>
> \(d\) a description of the **measures taken or proposed to be taken** by Processor to address the Personal Data Breach, including measures to contain the breach, mitigate its possible adverse effects, and prevent recurrence.

Where it is not possible to provide all of the above information at the time of the initial notification, Processor shall provide the information in phases without undue further delay, and shall provide updates at least every twelve (12) hours until the information is complete.

**11.3 Cooperation and Mitigation**

Upon becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach, Processor shall:

> \(i\) take immediate steps to investigate, contain, and mitigate the effects of the Personal Data Breach, including isolating affected systems, preserving forensic evidence, and implementing emergency security measures;
>
> \(ii\) cooperate fully with Controller in investigating the breach, including by providing all information, access, and assistance reasonably requested by Controller;
>
> \(iii\) cooperate with Controller in notifying affected Data Subjects and Supervisory Authorities as required by Applicable Data Protection Laws, including by providing information necessary for such notifications and by implementing notification logistics as directed by Controller;
>
> \(iv\) provide Controller with regular written updates on the status of the investigation and remediation efforts, at intervals of no less than every twenty-four (24) hours during the acute phase of the incident; and
>
> \(v\) not issue any public statement, press release, or other external communication regarding the Personal Data Breach without Controller\'s prior written consent, except as required by applicable law.

**11.4 HIPAA Breach Notification**

Without limiting the foregoing, Processor shall comply with the breach notification requirements applicable to Business Associates under 45 CFR § 164.410, including providing notice to Controller without unreasonable delay and in no case later than the timeline specified in Section 11.1 above (which the Parties acknowledge imposes a shorter timeline than the sixty (60) calendar day default period set out in 45 CFR § 164.410(b)). The notification shall include the identification of each individual whose unsecured PHI has been, or is reasonably believed by Processor to have been, accessed, acquired, used, or disclosed during the breach, to the extent such information is available.

**11.5 Record of Breaches**

Processor shall maintain a comprehensive record of all Personal Data Breaches, including a description of the facts relating to each breach, its effects, the remedial action taken, and the timeline of events. Processor shall make such record available to Controller upon request and in any event shall include a summary of all breaches during the preceding twelve (12) months in the annual compliance reporting provided to Controller.

**[SECTION 12: LIABILITY AND INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**

**12.1 Liability for Data Protection Breaches**

Processor\'s liability under this Agreement for any and all breaches of its data protection obligations (including, without limitation, obligations under Applicable Data Protection Laws, obligations as a Business Associate under HIPAA, and obligations relating to security, breach notification, sub-processing, international data transfers, data return and deletion, and restrictions on processing) shall not be subject to any general limitation of liability provision in the MSA. The Parties agree that data protection liability under this Agreement shall be subject to a minimum aggregate liability cap of **three (3) times the annual fees payable under the MSA** (calculated as 3 × \$18,600,000 = **\$55,800,000 (fifty-five million eight hundred thousand US dollars)**). For the avoidance of doubt, this liability cap represents a floor, not a ceiling, and nothing in this Agreement or the MSA shall reduce Processor\'s liability below this amount with respect to data protection obligations. This liability cap is separate from and in addition to any limitation of liability applicable to other obligations under the MSA.

**12.2 Indemnification by Processor**

Processor shall **indemnify, defend, and hold harmless** Controller, its affiliates (including Stratton Health UK Ltd.), and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and permitted assigns (collectively, the **\"Controller Indemnified Parties\"**) from and against any and all losses, liabilities, damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees, expert fees, court costs, and costs of investigation and remediation) arising from or relating to:

> \(a\) any breach of this Agreement by Processor or any of its Sub-Processors;
>
> \(b\) any third-party claims (including claims by Data Subjects, patients, healthcare providers, or consumer advocacy organizations) arising from or related to Processor\'s or its Sub-Processors\' breach of Applicable Data Protection Laws or this Agreement;
>
> \(c\) **regulatory fines, penalties, assessments, and enforcement actions** imposed on any Controller Indemnified Party by any Supervisory Authority, regulatory body, or governmental authority, to the extent that such fines, penalties, assessments, or enforcement actions are caused by or arise from Processor\'s or its Sub-Processors\' breach of this Agreement or Applicable Data Protection Laws, and to the extent that indemnification for such fines or penalties is legally permissible under the law governing the relevant regulatory action; and
>
> \(d\) any unauthorized Processing, use, disclosure, transfer, sale, or sharing of Personal Data by Processor or its Sub-Processors, or any Processing of Personal Data by Processor outside the scope of Controller\'s documented instructions.

**12.3 No Limitation for Willful Misconduct**

Nothing in this Agreement or the MSA shall limit either Party\'s liability for: (a) fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation; (b) willful misconduct; (c) gross negligence; or (d) death or personal injury caused by negligence. The limitations and exclusions of liability in this Agreement are without prejudice to any statutory liabilities that cannot be excluded or limited under applicable law.

**[SECTION 13: DATA RETURN AND DELETION]{.underline}**

**13.1 Return of Personal Data**

Upon termination or expiry of this Agreement or the MSA (whichever occurs first), or at any time upon Controller\'s written request, Processor shall return to Controller all Personal Data in Processor\'s possession or control, including all copies thereof and all data derived therefrom, in a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format. The format(s) for return shall include, at a minimum, CSV, JSON, and XML, or such other format(s) as Controller may reasonably specify. Processor shall complete the return of all Personal Data within **thirty (30) calendar days** of the effective date of termination or expiry, or of receipt of Controller\'s written request, as applicable. Processor shall cooperate with Controller and any successor service provider to ensure an orderly transition, including by providing reasonable technical assistance in migrating Personal Data.

**13.2 Deletion of Personal Data**

Following the return of Personal Data under Section 13.1, and upon written confirmation from Controller that the data has been successfully received, Processor shall securely delete or destroy all remaining copies of Personal Data in Processor\'s possession or control (including all backup copies, archived copies, copies in disaster recovery systems, and copies held by Sub-Processors) within **forty-five (45) calendar days** of the completion of the return. Deletion shall be performed using industry-standard methods that render the data permanently irrecoverable, in accordance with the National Institute of Standards and Technology Special Publication 800-88 Revision 1 (NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 1) guidelines for media sanitization, or an equivalent standard approved by Controller.

**13.3 Certification of Destruction**

Within ten (10) business days of the completion of deletion under Section 13.2, Processor shall provide Controller with a **written certification of destruction**, signed by an authorized officer of Processor at the level of Vice President or above, confirming:

> \(a\) the date(s) on which deletion was completed;
>
> \(b\) the categories of Personal Data deleted;
>
> \(c\) the deletion method(s) used, with sufficient detail to enable Controller to assess compliance with the NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 1 standard or equivalent; and
>
> \(d\) confirmation that no copies of the Personal Data remain in the possession or control of Processor or any of its Sub-Processors, in any form (including electronic, paper, or other media).

**13.4 Exceptions.** Processor may retain Personal Data (or specific portions thereof) to the extent, and for the duration, strictly required by applicable law, regulation, or order of a court or competent authority, provided that Processor:

> \(a\) informs Controller of such retention requirement promptly, and in any event within five (5) business days, including specifying the applicable legal obligation, the categories of Personal Data retained, and the expected duration of retention;
>
> \(b\) retains only the minimum data necessary to comply with the legal obligation;
>
> \(c\) continues to apply all protections of this Agreement (including the security measures set out in Section 8 and Annex 2 and the confidentiality obligations set out in Section 6) to any retained data for the duration of such retention; and
>
> \(d\) deletes the retained data promptly, and in any event within thirty (30) calendar days, upon the legal obligation ceasing to apply, and provides Controller with a supplemental certification of destruction in accordance with Section 13.3.

**[SECTION 14: GENERAL RESTRICTIONS ON PROCESSING]{.underline}**

**14.1 Purpose Limitation**

Processor shall Process Personal Data only for the specific purposes described in this Agreement and Annex 1 and only in accordance with Controller\'s documented instructions. Processor shall not Process Personal Data for any other purpose whatsoever, including but not limited to: (a) Processor\'s own business purposes; (b) product development, enhancement, or improvement; (c) analytics, benchmarking, or research (whether internal or external); (d) advertising, marketing, or promotional activities; (e) training of machine learning models or artificial intelligence systems; or (f) any purpose that is not directly related to the performance of the Services on behalf of Controller.

**14.2 Prohibition on Sale or Sharing**

Processor shall not sell Personal Data or share Personal Data for cross-context behavioral advertising purposes within the meaning of the CCPA/CPRA or any other Applicable Data Protection Law. Processor shall not combine Personal Data received from or on behalf of Controller with personal information that Processor receives from or on behalf of another person or entity, or that Processor collects from its own interaction with any Data Subject, except as expressly permitted by this Agreement and Applicable Data Protection Laws. Processor shall not disclose Personal Data to any third party for remuneration or other valuable consideration.

**[SECTION 15: INSURANCE]{.underline}**

**15.1 Cyber Insurance**

Processor shall, at its own cost, obtain and maintain throughout the entire Term of this Agreement (and for a period of not less than three (3) years following termination or expiry) a comprehensive cyber liability and technology errors and omissions insurance policy with a **minimum coverage of \$50,000,000 (fifty million US dollars) per occurrence** and **\$100,000,000 (one hundred million US dollars) in the aggregate** per policy year. The policy shall provide coverage for, at a minimum:

> \(a\) data breaches and privacy liability, including costs of investigation, notification, credit monitoring, and identity theft remediation;
>
> \(b\) network security liability, including liability for unauthorized access, malware, denial of service attacks, and transmission of viruses;
>
> \(c\) media liability;
>
> \(d\) regulatory defense costs and fines or penalties (to the extent insurable under applicable law);
>
> \(e\) crisis management and breach response costs, including forensic investigation, public relations, and call center services;
>
> \(f\) business interruption and data restoration costs; and
>
> \(g\) technology errors and omissions, including claims arising from failure to perform or negligent performance of the Services.

The policy shall name Controller and its affiliates (including Stratton Health UK Ltd.) as additional insureds. Processor shall provide Controller with a certificate of insurance evidencing such coverage within thirty (30) calendar days of the Effective Date and annually thereafter upon each renewal. The insurer shall have a financial strength rating of no less than \"A-\" (Excellent) as rated by AM Best or an equivalent rating by a nationally recognized rating organization. As of the Effective Date, Processor represents that its cyber liability and technology errors and omissions insurance is underwritten by Calloway National Insurance Group, with a current financial strength rating of \"A\" (Excellent) by AM Best.

**15.2 No Reduction in Coverage**

Processor shall not reduce the scope, limits, or terms of its insurance coverage below the minimum requirements set out in Section 15.1 without providing Controller with at least sixty (60) calendar days\' prior written notice. Any material reduction in coverage, including any reduction in per-occurrence or aggregate limits, any removal of named perils, or any increase in deductibles or retentions that would materially affect Controller\'s interests, shall entitle Controller to terminate this Agreement upon written notice.

**[SECTION 16: TERM AND TERMINATION]{.underline}**

**16.1 Term.** This Agreement shall come into effect on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and effect for the duration of the MSA (the **\"Term\"**). This Agreement shall automatically terminate upon the termination or expiry of the MSA, without the need for separate notice of termination by either Party. This Agreement is **co-terminus** with the MSA. The initial term of the MSA is five (5) years, commencing on March 3, 2025, and any renewal or extension of the MSA shall automatically extend the Term of this Agreement for a corresponding period.

**16.2 Early Termination**

Without prejudice to Controller\'s termination rights under the MSA, Controller may terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice to Processor if:

> \(a\) Processor is in material breach of any provision of this Agreement and fails to remedy such breach within thirty (30) calendar days of receiving written notice from Controller specifying the breach and requiring its remedy;
>
> \(b\) Processor breaches any provision of Applicable Data Protection Laws in a manner that materially affects, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, the Processing of Personal Data under this Agreement;
>
> \(c\) Processor undergoes a change of control (whether by merger, acquisition, sale of assets, or otherwise) that, in Controller\'s reasonable judgment, may adversely affect the protection of Personal Data;
>
> \(d\) Controller exercises its right to object to a proposed Sub-Processor under Section 7.3 and the Parties are unable to resolve the objection within the fifteen (15) day period specified therein; or
>
> \(e\) Processor becomes the subject of bankruptcy, insolvency, receivership, or similar proceedings.

**16.3 Effect of Termination**

Upon termination or expiry of this Agreement for any reason, Processor shall: (a) immediately cease all Processing of Personal Data except as strictly necessary to comply with Section 13 (Data Return and Deletion) or as otherwise directed by Controller; (b) comply with its obligations under Section 13 within the timeframes specified therein; and (c) provide reasonable cooperation and assistance to Controller in transitioning the Services to Controller or a replacement service provider, including providing reasonable technical support and access during the transition period.

**16.4 Survival.** The following provisions of this Agreement shall survive the termination or expiry of this Agreement and shall continue in full force and effect: Section 1 (Definitions and Interpretation), Section 6 (Confidentiality), Section 11 (Personal Data Breach Notification), Section 12 (Liability and Indemnification), Section 13 (Data Return and Deletion), Section 15 (Insurance, with respect to tail coverage for the three-year post-termination period), Section 17 (HIPAA Business Associate Provisions, to the extent obligations survive under HIPAA), Section 20 (Governing Law and Jurisdiction), and this Section 16.4.

**[SECTION 17: HIPAA BUSINESS ASSOCIATE PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

The provisions of this Section 17 apply to the extent that Processor creates, receives, maintains, or transmits PHI on behalf of Controller in the course of performing the Services. This Section 17 constitutes a Business Associate Agreement for purposes of HIPAA.

**17.1 Permitted Uses and Disclosures**

Processor, as a Business Associate of Controller, shall not use or disclose PHI other than as permitted or required by this Agreement or as required by law. Processor shall not use or disclose PHI in a manner that would violate the HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E) if done by Controller as a Covered Entity, except that Processor may use PHI for Processor\'s proper management and administration or to carry out its legal responsibilities, provided that:

> \(a\) the disclosures are required by law; or
>
> \(b\) Processor obtains reasonable assurances from the person to whom the information is disclosed that: (i) it will be held confidentially and used or further disclosed only as required by law or for the purposes for which it was disclosed to the person; and (ii) the person will notify Processor of any instances of which it becomes aware in which the confidentiality of the information has been breached.

**17.2 Safeguards.** Processor shall implement administrative, physical, and technical safeguards that reasonably and appropriately protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of ePHI that it creates, receives, maintains, or transmits on behalf of Controller, in accordance with the HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C). Processor shall comply with the requirements of 45 CFR § 164.306 (security standards), § 164.308 (administrative safeguards), § 164.310 (physical safeguards), § 164.312 (technical safeguards), and § 164.316 (policies and procedures and documentation requirements).

**17.3 Reporting.** Processor shall report to Controller any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this Agreement of which Processor becomes aware, including any Security Incident (as defined in 45 CFR § 164.304) and any Breach of Unsecured PHI (as defined in 45 CFR § 164.402), in accordance with the timelines and procedures set out in Section 11 of this Agreement.

**17.4 Sub-Contractors (HIPAA)**

In accordance with 45 CFR § 164.502(e)(1)(ii) and § 164.504(e)(2)(ii)(D), Processor shall ensure that any Sub-Processor or agent that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits PHI on behalf of Processor agrees in writing to the same restrictions, conditions, and requirements that apply to Processor under this Agreement with respect to such PHI. Each such written agreement with a Sub-Processor or agent shall satisfy the requirements of a Business Associate subcontractor agreement under HIPAA and shall be provided to Controller upon request.

**17.5 Access to PHI**

Processor shall, within ten (10) business days of a written request by Controller, make available PHI in a Designated Record Set (as defined in 45 CFR § 164.501) that is maintained by Processor, in order for Controller to provide individuals with access to their PHI in accordance with 45 CFR § 164.524. If Processor receives a request for access to PHI directly from a Data Subject, Processor shall forward such request to Controller within two (2) business days and shall not respond directly to the Data Subject without Controller\'s authorization.

**17.6 Amendments to PHI**

Processor shall, within ten (10) business days of a written request by Controller, incorporate any amendments to PHI in a Designated Record Set that is maintained by Processor, in accordance with 45 CFR § 164.526.

**17.7 Accounting of Disclosures**

Processor shall maintain and make available to Controller, within ten (10) business days of a written request, the information required for Controller to provide an accounting of disclosures of PHI in accordance with 45 CFR § 164.528. Processor shall maintain such information for a period of at least six (6) years from the date of the last disclosure to which the accounting relates.

**17.8 HHS Access**

Processor shall make its internal practices, books, and records relating to the use and disclosure of PHI available to the Secretary of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services for purposes of determining Controller\'s compliance with HIPAA and the HIPAA Rules. Processor shall promptly notify Controller of any such request or inquiry by the Secretary.

**17.9 Mitigation.** Processor shall mitigate, to the extent practicable, any harmful effect that is known to Processor of a use or disclosure of PHI by Processor or any of its Sub-Processors in violation of the requirements of this Agreement.

**17.10 Regulatory Changes**

The Parties acknowledge that HIPAA and its implementing regulations may be amended from time to time. The Parties shall amend this Agreement as necessary to comply with any changes to HIPAA regulations that affect the obligations of the Parties under this Agreement. To the extent that any HIPAA regulation referenced in this Agreement is amended, superseded, or replaced, the reference shall be deemed to be to such regulation as amended, superseded, or replaced, and Processor shall comply with the requirements of the amended regulation as of its effective date.

**[SECTION 18: CCPA/CPRA PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**18.1** For purposes of the CCPA/CPRA, Processor acts as a **\"Service Provider\"** as defined in California Civil Code § 1798.140(ag) with respect to any Personal Data that constitutes \"personal information\" under the CCPA/CPRA. Processor is prohibited from:

> \(a\) selling or sharing Personal Data within the meaning of California Civil Code § 1798.140(ad) and (ah);
>
> \(b\) retaining, using, or disclosing Personal Data for any purpose other than for the specific business purposes set forth in this Agreement, including retaining, using, or disclosing Personal Data for a commercial purpose other than providing the Services;
>
> \(c\) retaining, using, or disclosing Personal Data outside of the direct business relationship between Controller and Processor; and
>
> \(d\) combining Personal Data that Processor receives from or on behalf of Controller with personal information that it receives from or on behalf of another person or persons, or that it collects from its own interaction with any consumer, except to the extent expressly permitted by the CCPA/CPRA and approved by Controller in writing.

**18.2** Processor hereby certifies that it understands the restrictions set forth in this Section 18 and will comply with them. Processor further certifies that it will not take any action that would cause any transfer of Personal Data to Processor to qualify as a \"sale\" or \"sharing\" of personal information under the CCPA/CPRA.

**18.3** Controller shall have the right to take reasonable and appropriate steps to help ensure that Processor uses Personal Data in a manner consistent with Controller\'s obligations under the CCPA/CPRA, including by conducting audits and inspections as set out in Section 10 of this Agreement.

**18.4** If Processor determines that it can no longer meet its obligations under the CCPA/CPRA, Processor shall promptly notify Controller in writing and shall provide Controller with a description of the circumstances giving rise to such determination. Controller shall have the right to take reasonable and appropriate steps to stop and remediate unauthorized use of Personal Data.

**[SECTION 19: DATA PROTECTION IMPACT ASSESSMENTS]{.underline}**

**19.1** Processor shall provide reasonable assistance to Controller in the conduct of data protection impact assessments (**\"DPIAs\"**) under Article 35 of the EU GDPR and the UK GDPR, and in prior consultations with Supervisory Authorities under Article 36 of the EU GDPR and the UK GDPR, to the extent that such assessments or consultations relate to Processing activities performed by Processor under this Agreement.

**19.2** Such assistance shall include, without limitation, providing Controller with detailed information about Processor\'s Processing operations, technical and organizational security measures, risk assessments, data flows, system architecture, and any other information reasonably necessary for Controller to complete a DPIA or to respond to inquiries from a Supervisory Authority. Processor shall respond to requests for information under this Section 19 within ten (10) business days.

**[SECTION 20: GOVERNING LAW AND JURISDICTION]{.underline}**

**20.1 Governing Law**

This Agreement and any dispute or claim (including non-contractual disputes or claims) arising out of or in connection with this Agreement or its subject matter or formation shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the **laws of the State of Delaware, United States of America**, without regard to its conflict of laws principles or any choice of law rules that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

**20.2 Jurisdiction.** The Parties irrevocably submit to the **exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in the State of Delaware** (including the United States District Court for the District of Delaware and the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware) for the purpose of any suit, action, or other judicial proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement. Each Party irrevocably waives any objection it may have to the venue of any such suit, action, or proceeding in such courts, and any claim that any such suit, action, or proceeding has been brought in an inconvenient forum.

**20.3 Regulatory Jurisdiction**

Nothing in this Section 20 shall limit the right of any Supervisory Authority or regulatory body to exercise jurisdiction over the Processing of Personal Data in accordance with Applicable Data Protection Laws. The Parties acknowledge that multiple regulatory authorities may have concurrent jurisdiction over the Processing activities contemplated by this Agreement.

**[SECTION 21: NOTICES]{.underline}**

**21.1** All notices, requests, demands, and other communications under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed to have been duly given when delivered by email (with confirmation of receipt by the recipient), overnight courier (with tracking confirmation), or certified or registered mail (return receipt requested), to the following addresses:

Execution by electronic signature (including DocuSign or similar platforms) shall be deemed original execution for all purposes.
