**[ANNEX 1: PROCESSING DETAILS]{.underline}**

This Annex 1 forms part of the Data Processing Agreement between the Parties and describes the Processing of Personal Data by Processor on behalf of Controller.

**A1.1 Subject Matter and Duration of Processing**

**Subject Matter:** The hosting and provision of managed infrastructure services for the StrattonCare telemedicine platform, including cloud hosting, storage, backup, disaster recovery, infrastructure management, security monitoring, and related managed services as more particularly described in the MSA.

**Duration:** Processing shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue for the duration of the MSA (initial term of five (5) years commencing March 3, 2025), unless terminated earlier in accordance with Section 16 of this Agreement. Processing shall cease upon termination or expiry of this Agreement, subject to the data return and deletion obligations set out in Section 13.

**A1.2 Nature and Purpose of Processing**

**Nature of Processing:** Cloud hosting, storage, data backup and replication, disaster recovery, infrastructure management and monitoring, network security monitoring, patch management, system administration, log management, and other managed infrastructure services as set out in the MSA.

**Purpose of Processing:** To enable Controller to deliver telemedicine services (including virtual consultations, prescription management, patient record management, clinical workflow management, patient authentication, and payment processing) to patients and healthcare providers through the StrattonCare platform. Processing is carried out exclusively for the purpose of supporting Controller\'s delivery of the Services to Controller\'s end users and for no other purpose.

**A1.3 Types of Personal Data**

The following categories of Personal Data may be Processed by Processor in connection with the Services:

> \(a\) **Patient demographic data:** full name, date of birth, home address, Social Security Number (or other national identification number), telephone number(s), email address, gender, ethnicity (where voluntarily provided), emergency contact information;
>
> \(b\) **Clinical records and health data:** diagnoses, prescriptions, treatment plans, lab results, imaging reports, clinical notes, medication histories, allergy information, immunization records, referral information, and other records within the scope of Protected Health Information;
>
> \(c\) **Biometric identifiers:** voice prints used for patient authentication on the StrattonCare platform;
>
> \(d\) **Payment card data:** credit and debit card numbers, cardholder name, card expiration date, CVV/CVC codes, and transaction records (within the scope of PCI DSS);
>
> \(e\) **Behavioral and usage analytics:** login timestamps, session duration, feature usage patterns, device information (device type, operating system, browser), IP addresses, geolocation data (approximate), and cookie identifiers;
>
> \(f\) **Healthcare provider data:** full name, medical license number(s), specialty, Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) number, National Provider Identifier (NPI) number, professional credentials, employment history, and contact information; and
>
> \(g\) **Communications data:** telemedicine session recordings (audio and video), secure messages between patients and providers, chat transcripts, and appointment scheduling communications.

**A1.4 Categories of Data Subjects**

The following categories of Data Subjects may have their Personal Data Processed by Processor:

> \(a\) **Patients:** approximately 2,300,000 US patients and approximately 14,000 EU/UK patients registered on the StrattonCare platform;
>
> \(b\) **Healthcare providers:** approximately 6,200 physicians, nurses, and allied health professionals who provide services through the StrattonCare platform; and
>
> \(c\) **Administrative users:** Controller\'s employees and contractors who access the StrattonCare platform for administrative, operational, or support purposes.

**Total estimated Data Subjects:** approximately 2,320,200 individuals.

**A1.5 Permitted Processing Locations**

> \(a\) **London, United Kingdom** --- CloudNest UK Data Center, Docklands Campus
>
> \(b\) **Frankfurt, Germany** --- CloudNest EU Data Center, Frankfurt-Rödelheim Campus

No other processing locations are authorized without Controller\'s prior written consent in accordance with Section 5 of this Agreement.

**A1.6 Controller\'s Data Protection Contact**

Anisha Ramachandran, Chief Privacy Officer Stratton Health Technologies, Inc. 900 Lakeview Boulevard, Suite 1500, Austin, TX 78701

Email: a.ramachandran@strattonhealth.com

**A1.7 Processor\'s Data Protection Contact**

Dr. Henrik Lindqvist, Data Protection Officer CloudNest Infrastructure Services Ltd. 45 Canary Wharf Tower, Level 22, London E14 5AB, United Kingdom

Email: h.lindqvist@cloudnest.co.uk

**[ANNEX 2: TECHNICAL AND ORGANIZATIONAL SECURITY MEASURES]{.underline}**

This Annex 2 forms part of the Data Processing Agreement between the Parties and sets out the minimum technical and organizational security measures that Processor shall implement and maintain throughout the Term of this Agreement.

**A2.1 Encryption.**

> \(a\) **Data at rest:** All Personal Data stored on Processor\'s systems shall be encrypted using AES-256 encryption (or a cryptographically equivalent or stronger standard).
>
> \(b\) **Data in transit:** All transmissions of Personal Data shall be encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher. Unencrypted transmission of Personal Data is prohibited.
>
> \(c\) **Key management:** Encryption keys shall be stored in FIPS 140-2 Level 3 (or higher) certified hardware security modules (HSMs). Encryption keys shall be rotated at least annually and immediately upon any suspected compromise. Key management procedures shall be documented and subject to regular review.

**A2.2 Access Controls**

> \(a\) Role-based access control (RBAC) shall be implemented with the principle of least privilege, ensuring that personnel are granted only the minimum level of access necessary to perform their assigned duties.
>
> \(b\) Multi-factor authentication (MFA) shall be required for all personnel accessing systems, networks, or applications that contain or may be used to access Personal Data.
>
> \(c\) Access reviews shall be conducted at least quarterly to verify that access privileges remain appropriate and that access for terminated or reassigned personnel has been revoked.
>
> \(d\) Automated deprovisioning procedures shall ensure that access is revoked within twenty-four (24) hours of personnel termination or role change.
>
> \(e\) Privileged access (administrative and root accounts) shall be subject to enhanced monitoring and shall be logged and reviewed.

**A2.3 Network Security**

> \(a\) Firewalls, intrusion detection systems (IDS), and intrusion prevention systems (IPS) shall be deployed and maintained at all network perimeters and critical internal segments.
>
> \(b\) Network segmentation shall be implemented to isolate Controller\'s environment from other customers and from Processor\'s corporate network.
>
> \(c\) Distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) protection shall be in place for all externally facing services.
>
> \(d\) Vulnerability scanning shall be conducted at least monthly, and all critical and high-severity vulnerabilities shall be remediated within thirty (30) calendar days of discovery.
>
> \(e\) Penetration testing shall be conducted at least annually by a qualified independent third party, and results shall be shared with Controller.

**A2.4 Physical Security**

> \(a\) Data centers shall be secured with biometric access controls (e.g., fingerprint, iris scan), proximity card readers, and mantrap entry systems.
>
> \(b\) 24/7 closed-circuit television (CCTV) monitoring shall be in place at all data center facilities, with footage retained for a minimum of ninety (90) days.
>
> \(c\) On-site security personnel shall be present 24/7 at all data center facilities.
>
> \(d\) Environmental controls shall include fire detection and suppression systems, climate control (temperature and humidity), uninterruptible power supply (UPS), and backup diesel generators with minimum 72-hour fuel capacity.
>
> \(e\) Visitor access logs shall be maintained for a minimum of twelve (12) months. All visitors shall be escorted at all times within secure areas.

**A2.5 Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery**

> \(a\) Redundant infrastructure shall be maintained across Permitted Processing Locations to ensure continuity of service in the event of a facility-level failure.
>
> \(b\) **Recovery Point Objective (RPO):** One (1) hour.
>
> \(c\) **Recovery Time Objective (RTO):** Four (4) hours.
>
> \(d\) Disaster recovery plans shall be tested at least annually, and test results (including any identified gaps and remediation actions) shall be shared with Controller within thirty (30) calendar days of each test.

**A2.6 Logging and Monitoring**

> \(a\) Comprehensive audit logging shall be implemented for all access to, and actions performed on, systems containing Personal Data, including authentication events, data access, data modification, data deletion, and administrative actions.
>
> \(b\) Logs shall be retained for a minimum of twenty-four (24) months and shall be protected against unauthorized modification or deletion.
>
> \(c\) A security information and event management (SIEM) system shall be in place with 24/7 monitoring by Processor\'s security operations center (SOC).
>
> \(d\) Anomaly detection and automated alerting shall be implemented for suspicious activities, including unusual access patterns, data exfiltration indicators, and privilege escalation attempts.

**A2.7 Personnel Security**

> \(a\) Background checks (including criminal history, employment verification, and reference checks) shall be conducted for all personnel with access to Personal Data, prior to granting access.
>
> \(b\) Annual security awareness training shall be mandatory for all personnel, with specialized training for personnel handling PHI, Biometric Data, or payment card data.
>
> \(c\) Written confidentiality agreements shall be signed by all personnel prior to being granted access to Personal Data.
>
> \(d\) Documented disciplinary procedures shall be in place for security policy violations, including termination of access and, where appropriate, termination of employment.

**A2.8 Data Backup**

> \(a\) Encrypted backups of all Personal Data shall be performed daily.
>
> \(b\) Backups shall be stored in geographically separate but Permitted Processing Locations (i.e., within the EEA, UK, or US only).
>
> \(c\) Backup restoration testing shall be performed at least quarterly to verify the integrity and recoverability of backup data.
>
> \(d\) Backup media shall be subject to the same access controls and encryption standards as production data.

**A2.9 Incident Response**

> \(a\) A documented incident response plan shall be maintained and tested at least annually through tabletop exercises or simulated incident scenarios.
>
> \(b\) A designated incident response team shall be in place with clearly defined roles and responsibilities.
>
> \(c\) Escalation procedures and communication protocols shall be aligned with the notification requirements set out in Section 11 of this Agreement.
>
> \(d\) Post-incident reviews shall be conducted within fourteen (14) calendar days of incident resolution, and lessons learned shall be incorporated into security procedures.

**A2.10 Secure Development**

> \(a\) Secure software development lifecycle (SDLC) practices shall be followed for all software and infrastructure components used to Process Personal Data.
>
> \(b\) Code reviews and security testing (including static and dynamic application security testing) shall be performed prior to deployment of any changes to production systems.
>
> \(c\) Patch management procedures shall ensure that critical security patches are applied within twenty-four (24) hours of release by the applicable vendor, and that high-severity patches are applied within seven (7) calendar days.
>
> \(d\) Change management procedures shall be documented, and all changes to production systems shall be reviewed, approved, and logged.

**[ANNEX 3: APPROVED SUB-PROCESSORS]{.underline}**

This Annex 3 forms part of the Data Processing Agreement between the Parties and lists the Sub-Processors approved by Controller as of the Effective Date.

**A3.1 List of Approved Sub-Processors**

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Sub-Processor Name**   **Registered Address**   **Processing Activities**   **Processing Location(s)**   **Date of Approval**
  ------------------------ ------------------------ --------------------------- ---------------------------- ----------------------
  *None*                   *---*                    *---*                       *---*                        *---*

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**As of the Effective Date, no Sub-Processors have been approved by Controller.** Any engagement of a Sub-Processor by Processor must comply with the requirements of Section 7 of this Agreement, including obtaining Controller\'s prior specific written consent for each proposed Sub-Processor. This Annex 3 shall be updated from time to time by the mutual written agreement of the Parties to reflect any Sub-Processors subsequently approved by Controller.

**[ANNEX 4: INTERNATIONAL DATA TRANSFER MECHANISMS]{.underline}**

This Annex 4 forms part of the Data Processing Agreement between the Parties and sets out the mechanisms for international transfers of Personal Data, to the extent such transfers are authorized by Controller under Section 5.

**A4.1 Standard Contractual Clauses**

Where Personal Data originating in the EEA is transferred to a country outside the EEA that has not received an adequacy decision from the European Commission pursuant to Article 45 of the EU GDPR, the Standard Contractual Clauses approved by the European Commission pursuant to Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914 of 4 June 2021 (**Module Two: Controller to Processor**) shall apply and are hereby incorporated by reference into this Agreement.

Where Personal Data originating in the United Kingdom is transferred to a country outside the United Kingdom that has not been designated as providing an adequate level of protection by the UK Secretary of State, the UK International Data Transfer Addendum to the EU SCCs (as issued by the UK Information Commissioner\'s Office on 2 February 2022, version B1.0) shall also apply and is hereby incorporated by reference into this Agreement.

The SCCs shall be deemed completed as follows:

> **Clause 7 (Docking clause):** The optional docking clause is included.
>
> **Clause 9(a) (Sub-processor authorization):** Option 1 (prior specific authorization) is selected, consistent with Section 7.1 of this Agreement.
>
> **Clause 11 (Redress):** The optional redress clause is included.
>
> **Clause 13 (Supervision):** The competent supervisory authority shall be the supervisory authority of the EU member state in which Stratton Health UK Ltd. or the relevant EU Data Subjects are located, or the Irish Data Protection Commission where the relevant Data Subjects are located in multiple member states.
>
> **Clause 17 (Governing law):** The laws of Ireland shall govern the SCCs.
>
> **Clause 18 (Choice of forum and jurisdiction):** The courts of Ireland shall have jurisdiction.
>
> **Annex I (List of Parties):**
>
> • Data exporter (Controller): Stratton Health Technologies, Inc. (and its subsidiary, Stratton Health UK Ltd.)
>
> • Data importer (Processor): CloudNest Infrastructure Services Ltd.
>
> **Annex II (Technical and organizational measures):** As set out in Annex 2 of this Agreement.
>
> **Annex III (List of sub-processors):** As set out in Annex 3 of this Agreement (as updated from time to time).

**Note:** As of the Effective Date, no international data transfers requiring reliance on the SCCs are contemplated, as all Processing is restricted to the United Kingdom (London) and Germany (Frankfurt), both of which are within the UK and EEA respectively. This Annex 4 is included as a contingency mechanism in the event that additional processing locations are authorized by Controller under Section 5 in the future.

**A4.2 Supplementary Measures**

Where the SCCs are relied upon for any international transfer, the Parties shall implement such supplementary technical, organizational, and contractual measures as are necessary to ensure that the level of protection afforded to Personal Data is essentially equivalent to that guaranteed within the EEA and the United Kingdom, taking into account the laws and government access practices of the destination country, in accordance with the guidance of the European Data Protection Board (EDPB Recommendations 01/2020 on measures that supplement transfer tools to ensure compliance with the EU level of protection of personal data, as adopted on 18 June 2021) and the UK Information Commissioner\'s Office (International Data Transfer Agreement guidance).

**A4.3 Transfer Impact Assessments**

Processor shall cooperate fully with Controller in conducting any transfer impact assessment required under Section 5.3 of this Agreement. Such cooperation shall include, without limitation, providing Controller with: (a) detailed information about the legal framework of the destination country, including laws and regulations relating to government surveillance, law enforcement access, and national security; (b) information about Processor\'s or the relevant Sub-Processor\'s experience with government access requests in the destination country; (c) an assessment of the technical measures in place to protect Personal Data against unauthorized government access; and (d) any other information reasonably necessary for Controller to evaluate whether the transfer provides an essentially equivalent level of protection. Controller shall have sole discretion in determining whether a transfer may proceed based on the results of the transfer impact assessment.

1	CONFIDENTIAL — SUBJECT TO CONTRACT
2	DATA PROCESSING AGREEMENT
3	Entered into pursuant to the Master Services Agreement dated March 3, 2025
4	BETWEEN:
5	(1) Stratton Health Technologies, Inc., a corporation organized and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware, United States of America, with its principal offices located at 900 Lakeview Boulevard, Suite 1500, Austin, TX 78701 (hereinafter referred to as the "Controller" or "Stratton Health"); and
6	(2) CloudNest Infrastructure Services Ltd., a company incorporated in England and Wales under Company Number 11482937, with its registered office at 45 Canary Wharf Tower, Level 22, London E14 5AB, United Kingdom (hereinafter referred to as the "Processor" or "CloudNest").
7	** [[INS id=0 by Author: Each a "Party" and together the "Parties."]]
8	Effective Date: March 3, 2025 (the "Effective Date"), being the date of the Master Services Agreement entered into between the Parties (the "MSA").
9	Background: The Controller and the Processor have entered into a Master Services Agreement dated March 3, 2025 (the "MSA"), pursuant to which the Processor will provide cloud infrastructure and managed services to the Controller. This Data Processing Agreement (the "DPA") sets out the terms and conditions governing the Processor's processing of Personal Data on behalf of the Controller in connection with the provision of services under the MSA.
10	RECITALS
11	WHEREAS Stratton Health operates the "StrattonCare" telemedicine platform, a comprehensive digital health solution serving approximately 2.3 million patients across 38 states of the United States of America and approximately 14,000 patients in the European Union and the United Kingdom through its subsidiary, Stratton Health UK Ltd.;
12	WHEREAS the StrattonCare platform processes protected health information ("PHI"), personally identifiable information ("PII"), biometric identifiers (including voice prints used for patient authentication), payment card data subject to the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard, and behavioral and usage analytics data;
13	WHEREAS CloudNest provides cloud infrastructure and managed services and will host the StrattonCare platform on dedicated infrastructure in accordance with the terms of the MSA;
14	WHEREAS the Parties executed a Master Services Agreement dated March 3, 2025 (the "MSA") with a term of five (5) years and annual fees of $18,600,000 (eighteen million six hundred thousand US dollars);
15	WHEREAS the MSA contemplates this Data Processing Agreement to govern the processing of Personal Data by the Processor on behalf of the Controller in connection with the provision of services under the MSA;
16	WHEREAS the Parties wish to ensure compliance with all applicable data protection laws and regulations, including but not limited to the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 ("HIPAA"), the General Data Protection Regulation (EU) 2016/679 ("GDPR"), the UK Data Protection Act 2018 and UK GDPR, the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act ("CCPA/CPRA"), the Texas Data Privacy and Security Act ("TDPSA"), and the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard version 4.0 ("PCI DSS v4.0");
17	** [[INS id=1 by Author: WHEREAS CloudNest maintains robust data protection and security practices and certifications, including ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II, and processes data for healthcare, fintech, and government clients globally;]]
18	[COMMENT PV-01: "Added background recital to reflect CloudNest's established credentials and experience in regulated sectors. This provides helpful context for the security and compliance provisions below."]
19	NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual promises, covenants, and conditions set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
20	SECTION 1 — DEFINITIONS
21	1.1 In this DPA, unless the context otherwise requires, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this DPA shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the MSA.
22	(a) "Applicable Data Protection Law" means all laws and regulations applicable to the processing of Personal Data under this DPA, including but not limited to the GDPR, UK GDPR, UK Data Protection Act 2018, HIPAA (including the HITECH Act and all implementing regulations), CCPA/CPRA, TDPSA, and PCI DSS v4.0, in each case as amended, supplemented, or replaced from time to time.
23	(b) "Business Associate Agreement" or "BAA" means the business associate provisions incorporated into this DPA pursuant to Section 16, establishing the obligations of the Processor as a Business Associate of the Controller under HIPAA.
24	(c) "Controller" means Stratton Health Technologies, Inc.
25	(d) "Data Subject" means any identified or identifiable natural person whose Personal Data is processed under or in connection with this DPA.
26	(e) "EEA" means the European Economic Area (comprising the Member States of the European Union together with Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway).
27	(f) "MSA" means the Master Services Agreement entered into between the Parties dated March 3, 2025.
28	** (g) "Personal Data" means [[DEL id=2: any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person as defined under Applicable Data Protection Law]] [[INS id=3 by Author: any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person, including pseudonymized data and metadata that could directly or indirectly identify a natural person when combined with other information available to the Controller or Processor, as defined under Applicable Data Protection Law]].
29	[COMMENT PV-02: "We have broadened the definition of Personal Data to ensure pseudonymized and combinable metadata are expressly covered. CloudNest believes this broader scope ensures comprehensive protection."]
30	(h) "Personal Data Breach" means a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorized disclosure of, or access to, Personal Data transmitted, stored, or otherwise processed, as defined in Article 4(12) of the GDPR.
31	(i) "Processor" means CloudNest Infrastructure Services Ltd.
32	(j) "Processing" means any operation or set of operations which is performed on Personal Data or on sets of Personal Data, whether or not by automated means, such as collection, recording, organization, structuring, storage, adaptation or alteration, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure by transmission, dissemination or otherwise making available, alignment or combination, restriction, erasure, or destruction, as defined in Article 4(2) of the GDPR.
33	(k) "Sub-Processor" means any third party engaged by the Processor (or by any subsequent Sub-Processor of the Processor) to carry out Processing activities in respect of Personal Data on behalf of the Controller.
34	(l) "Standard Contractual Clauses" or "SCCs" means the standard contractual clauses for the transfer of personal data to third countries approved by the European Commission pursuant to Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914 of 4 June 2021, and/or the UK International Data Transfer Addendum issued by the Information Commissioner's Office, as applicable.
35	(m) "PHI" means Protected Health Information as defined in 45 C.F.R. § 160.103.
36	** [[INS id=4 by Author: (n) "Anonymized Data" means Personal Data that has been processed in such a manner that it can no longer be attributed to a specific Data Subject without the use of additional information, provided that such additional information is kept separately.]]
37	[COMMENT PV-03: "Added definition of 'Anonymized Data' to support new Section 14.3 below. This aligns with standard industry practice for data improvement activities."]
38	1.2 References to any statute, statutory provision, or regulation shall include any modification, re-enactment, or successor legislation, and all subordinate legislation made from time to time under the relevant statute or statutory provision. Words importing the singular shall include the plural and vice versa, and words importing any gender shall include all genders.
39	SECTION 2 — SCOPE AND APPLICABILITY
40	2.1 This DPA governs the processing of Personal Data by the Processor on behalf of the Controller in connection with the provision of services under the MSA. The terms of this DPA shall apply to all Processing of Personal Data carried out by or on behalf of the Processor in the performance of the MSA.
41	2.2 This DPA incorporates and includes the obligations of a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement as set forth in Section 16. To the extent that the Processor processes PHI on behalf of the Controller, the Business Associate provisions in Section 16 shall apply in addition to, and without limitation of, the other provisions of this DPA.
42	2.3 This DPA applies to all Personal Data processed in connection with the StrattonCare platform, including but not limited to patient data, healthcare provider data, clinical records, biometric identifiers, payment card data, and behavioral and usage analytics, as further described in Annex 1.
43	2.4 In the event of any conflict between the provisions of this DPA and the provisions of the MSA, the provisions of this DPA shall prevail with respect to the processing of Personal Data. In the event of any conflict between the body of this DPA and the Annexes, the body of this DPA shall prevail.
44	SECTION 3 — ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
45	3.1 The Parties acknowledge and agree that, with respect to the processing of Personal Data under this DPA, Stratton Health is the Controller (and Covered Entity under HIPAA) and CloudNest is the Processor (and Business Associate under HIPAA).
46	** 3.2 The Processor shall process Personal Data only on documented instructions from the Controller, including with regard to transfers of Personal Data to a third country or an international organization[[INS id=5 by Author: , unless required to do so by applicable law to which the Processor is subject, in which case the Processor shall inform the Controller of that legal requirement before processing, unless that law prohibits such information on important grounds of public interest]].
47	[COMMENT PV-04: "Standard carve-out per GDPR Art. 28(3)(a). Processor may be subject to UK/EU legal requirements mandating processing."]
48	3.3 The Processor shall immediately inform the Controller if, in the Processor's opinion, an instruction from the Controller infringes Applicable Data Protection Law. The Processor shall not be required to carry out processing that it reasonably believes would infringe Applicable Data Protection Law, provided that it promptly notifies the Controller and documents its reasons for such belief.
49	3.4 The Controller shall be responsible for ensuring that the processing of Personal Data under this DPA has a lawful basis under Applicable Data Protection Law, including obtaining any necessary consents or authorizations from Data Subjects where required.
50	SECTION 4 — DETAILS OF PROCESSING
51	4.1 Subject Matter. The subject matter of the Processing is the hosting and provision of managed services for the StrattonCare telemedicine platform in accordance with the MSA.
52	** 4.2 Duration. The duration of the Processing shall be [[DEL id=6: co-terminus with the MSA]] [[INS id=7 by Author: as set forth in Section 18 (Term and Termination)]].
53	** 4.3 Nature of Processing. The nature of the Processing includes storage, hosting, backup, disaster recovery, technical support, [[INS id=8 by Author: log analytics and performance monitoring,]] and such other processing activities as are necessary for the Processor to perform its obligations under the MSA.
54	4.4 Purpose of Processing. The purpose of the Processing is the provision of services by the Processor to the Controller under the MSA, including the hosting, maintenance, and support of the StrattonCare platform.
55	4.5 Categories of Data Subjects. The Personal Data processed under this DPA relates to the following categories of Data Subjects:
56	(a) Patients of the StrattonCare platform (approximately 2.3 million in the United States and approximately 14,000 in the European Union and United Kingdom);
57	(b) Healthcare providers using the StrattonCare platform (approximately 6,200 physicians, nurses, and allied health professionals).
58	4.6 Categories of Personal Data. The categories of Personal Data processed under this DPA include:
59	(a) Patient demographic data (name, date of birth, address, Social Security number or national identification number, telephone number, email address);
60	(b) Clinical records (diagnoses, prescriptions, laboratory results, imaging reports, clinical notes, treatment plans);
61	(c) Biometric identifiers (voice prints used for patient authentication);
62	(d) Payment card data (credit and debit card numbers, expiration dates, security codes, billing information);
63	(e) Behavioral and usage analytics (platform interaction data, session logs, device information, IP addresses).
64	4.7 Special Categories and Sensitive Data. The Processing includes the following special categories of data and sensitive data: health data within the meaning of Article 9 of the GDPR; biometric data within the meaning of Article 9 of the GDPR; and Protected Health Information as defined under HIPAA.
65	4.8 Further details of the Processing activities are set forth in Annex 1 to this DPA.
66	SECTION 5 — PROCESSOR'S OBLIGATIONS
67	5.1 The Processor shall treat all Personal Data as confidential and shall ensure that any natural person acting under its authority who has access to Personal Data does not process such data except on instructions from the Controller, unless required to do so by Applicable Data Protection Law.
68	5.2 The Processor shall ensure that all personnel authorized to process Personal Data have committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality. The Processor shall ensure that access to Personal Data is limited to those personnel who require access in order to perform the Processor's obligations under the MSA and this DPA.
69	5.3 The Processor shall immediately inform the Controller if, in the Processor's opinion, an instruction from the Controller infringes any Applicable Data Protection Law, and shall provide sufficient detail to enable the Controller to assess the basis for such opinion.
70	** [[INS id=9 by Author: 5.4 Controller shall maintain the confidentiality of all information relating to Processor's security architecture, infrastructure configurations, and proprietary technical measures disclosed in connection with this DPA or any audit conducted hereunder, and shall not disclose such information to any third party without Processor's prior written consent, except as required by applicable law or regulation.]]
71	[COMMENT PV-05: "Mutual confidentiality for security architecture is industry-standard. Disclosure of CloudNest's security configurations could create vulnerabilities."]
72	5.5 The Processor shall provide reasonable assistance to the Controller in conducting data protection impact assessments ("DPIAs") where required under Article 35 of the GDPR or equivalent provisions of Applicable Data Protection Law, taking into account the nature of the Processing and the information available to the Processor.
73	SECTION 6 — SECURITY MEASURES
74	** 6.1 The Processor shall implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk, including the measures set forth in Annex 2. [[DEL id=10: Processor shall comply with the security requirements specified in Annex 2 at all times during the term of this DPA.]] [[INS id=11 by Author: Processor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to comply with the security requirements specified in Annex 2 during the term of this DPA.]]
75	** [[INS id=12 by Author: 6.2 Processor's security obligations under this Section 6 and Annex 2 shall be deemed satisfied where Processor has implemented security measures substantially consistent with industry standards for cloud infrastructure providers of similar size and scope.]]
76	[COMMENT PV-06: "CloudNest's security program exceeds industry norms. The 'commercially reasonable efforts' standard reflects the dynamic nature of cybersecurity — absolute compliance warranties are impractical given evolving threat landscapes. The industry-standard benchmark provides an objective, defensible standard."]
77	6.3 The Processor shall ensure that any personnel processing Personal Data have been informed of the confidential nature of the Personal Data and have undertaken appropriate confidentiality obligations. The Processor shall ensure that its personnel receive appropriate training on data protection and information security, commensurate with their roles and responsibilities.
78	6.4 Without prejudice to the generality of Section 6.1, the Processor shall implement and maintain the specific technical and organizational measures set forth in Annex 2, including but not limited to:
79	(a) encryption of Personal Data at rest using AES-256 or equivalent standard;
80	(b) encryption of Personal Data in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher;
81	(c) role-based access controls applying the principle of least privilege;
82	(d) multi-factor authentication for all administrative and privileged access;
83	(e) intrusion detection and prevention systems;
84	(f) regular vulnerability scanning and annual penetration testing by independent third parties;
85	(g) physical security measures for all data center facilities;
86	(h) business continuity and disaster recovery procedures.
87	6.5 The Processor shall regularly test, assess, and evaluate the effectiveness of its technical and organizational measures for ensuring the security of Processing, and shall make improvements to such measures as necessary to maintain an appropriate level of security, taking into account the state of the art, the costs of implementation, and the nature, scope, context, and purposes of Processing, as well as the risks of varying likelihood and severity for the rights and freedoms of natural persons.
88	SECTION 7 — SUB-PROCESSING
89	** 7.1 [[DEL id=13: Processor shall not engage any Sub-Processor to carry out Processing activities on behalf of Controller without obtaining the prior specific written consent of Controller for each Sub-Processor.]] [[INS id=14 by Author: Controller hereby provides general written authorization for Processor to engage Sub-Processors to carry out Processing activities on behalf of Controller, subject to the conditions set forth in this Section 7. Processor shall maintain an up-to-date list of Sub-Processors, which as of the Effective Date is set forth in Annex 3.]]
90	** 7.2 [[DEL id=15: Processor shall notify Controller in writing at least thirty (30) days in advance of any intended addition or replacement of a Sub-Processor]] [[INS id=16 by Author: Processor shall notify Controller in writing at least fifteen (15) days in advance of any intended addition or replacement of a Sub-Processor]], providing the identity of the proposed Sub-Processor, the nature of the Processing to be carried out, and the location of the Processing.
91	** 7.3 [[DEL id=17: Controller shall have the right to object to the appointment of a new Sub-Processor by notifying Processor in writing within fifteen (15) days of receipt of Processor's notice. If Controller objects and the Parties are unable to resolve the objection within fifteen (15) days of Controller's notice of objection, Controller shall have the right to terminate this DPA and the relevant portions of the MSA without penalty.]] [[INS id=18 by Author: Controller may raise reasonable concerns regarding a new Sub-Processor, and Processor shall consider such concerns in good faith.]]
92	[COMMENT PV-07: "General authorization model with maintained list is the prevailing market standard for cloud infrastructure providers and is expressly contemplated by GDPR Art. 28(2). The 15-day notice period provides sufficient time for Controller review. The good-faith consultation mechanism ensures Controller's concerns are heard while avoiding unworkable unilateral veto rights that could disrupt service delivery."]
93	7.4 The Processor shall ensure that each Sub-Processor is bound by a written agreement imposing data protection obligations no less onerous than those set forth in this DPA, including in particular providing sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organizational measures in such a manner that the Processing will meet the requirements of Applicable Data Protection Law. The Processor shall provide copies of Sub-Processor agreements to the Controller upon reasonable request.
94	7.5 The Processor shall remain fully liable to the Controller for the acts and omissions of its Sub-Processors as if such acts and omissions were those of the Processor itself. The engagement of a Sub-Processor shall not relieve the Processor of any obligation under this DPA.
95	SECTION 8 — INTERNATIONAL DATA TRANSFERS
96	** 8.1 [[DEL id=19: Processor shall not transfer or process Personal Data outside of the European Economic Area ("EEA"), the United Kingdom, or the United States of America without the prior written consent of Controller. Any such transfer shall be subject to appropriate safeguards, including Standard Contractual Clauses approved by the European Commission or UK Information Commissioner's Office, as applicable.]] [[INS id=20 by Author: Processor shall process Personal Data in the locations set forth in Annex 1, Section 3 ("Approved Processing Locations"). As of the Effective Date, the Approved Processing Locations are: London, United Kingdom; Frankfurt, Germany; and Mumbai, India.]]
97	** [[INS id=21 by Author: 8.2 Where Personal Data is transferred to a Processing location outside the EEA or United Kingdom, Processor shall ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place in accordance with Applicable Data Protection Law.]]
98	[COMMENT PV-08: "CloudNest's existing sub-processor Peregrine Data Analytics Pvt. Ltd. operates from Mumbai and provides essential log analytics and performance monitoring services. This processing is limited to technical operational data and is integral to CloudNest's managed services offering. The Mumbai location has been added to the Approved Processing Locations to reflect current operational reality."]
99	8.3 The Standard Contractual Clauses adopted by the European Commission and the UK International Data Transfer Addendum, as set forth in Annex 4, shall be incorporated by reference where required for international transfers of Personal Data.
100	** [[DEL id=22: 8.4 Controller shall have the right to approve or reject any proposed transfer mechanism prior to any international transfer of Personal Data.]]
101	SECTION 9 — DATA SUBJECT RIGHTS
102	9.1 The Processor shall, taking into account the nature of the Processing, assist the Controller by appropriate technical and organizational measures, insofar as this is possible, for the fulfillment of the Controller's obligation to respond to requests for exercising the Data Subject's rights under Applicable Data Protection Law, including but not limited to rights of access, rectification, erasure, data portability, restriction of Processing, and objection.
103	** 9.2 The Processor shall, within [[DEL id=23: five (5)]] [[INS id=24 by Author: fifteen (15)]] business days of receiving a forwarded data subject request from Controller, provide such assistance as is reasonably necessary to enable Controller to respond to the request.
104	** [[INS id=25 by Author: 9.3 Where the volume of data subject requests forwarded by Controller exceeds ten (10) requests in any calendar month, Controller shall reimburse Processor for the reasonable costs incurred by Processor in providing assistance with such excess requests. Processor shall provide Controller with reasonable documentation of costs incurred.]]
105	[COMMENT PV-09: "The 15 business day timeline reflects operational realities of locating and compiling data across distributed cloud infrastructure. The fee provision for high-volume requests is consistent with GDPR Art. 28(3), which permits the Processor to charge a reasonable fee. The threshold of 10 requests per month is generous for the anticipated volume."]
106	9.4 The Processor shall notify the Controller promptly, and in any event within three (3) business days, if it receives a data subject request directly. The Processor shall not respond to any data subject request directly unless expressly authorized to do so in writing by the Controller.
107	9.5 The Processor shall maintain adequate systems and processes to enable it to locate and retrieve Personal Data relating to an individual Data Subject across all systems and environments in which Controller Personal Data is processed, for the purpose of facilitating the exercise of Data Subject rights.
108	SECTION 10 — PERSONAL DATA BREACH NOTIFICATION
109	** 10.1 [[DEL id=26: Processor shall notify Controller without undue delay and in any event within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting Controller's Personal Data.]] [[INS id=27 by Author: Processor shall notify Controller without undue delay and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours of confirming that a security incident constitutes a Personal Data Breach affecting Controller's Personal Data.]]
110	10.2 The notification under Section 10.1 shall include, to the extent reasonably available at the time of notification:
111	[DELETED: (i) the nature of the Personal Data Breach, including the categories and approximate number of Data Subjects concerned;
112	(ii) the approximate number of Personal Data records concerned;
113	(iii) the likely consequences of the Personal Data Breach;
114	(iv) the measures taken or proposed to be taken by Processor to address the Personal Data Breach, including measures to mitigate its possible adverse effects.]
115	[ADDED: (i) the nature of the Personal Data Breach, including where possible the categories of Data Subjects concerned;
116	(ii) the likely consequences of the Personal Data Breach; and
117	(iii) the name and contact details of Processor's Data Protection Officer or other contact point from whom more information may be obtained.]
118	[COMMENT PV-10: "The 72-hour notification window aligns with GDPR Art. 33(1) controller notification obligations to supervisory authorities. The trigger of 'confirming' rather than 'becoming aware' avoids premature notifications for suspected but unverified incidents, which could cause unnecessary alarm and resource expenditure. The streamlined content requirements avoid delay caused by compiling detailed information before initial notification — follow-up notifications can provide additional detail as investigation progresses."]
119	10.3 The Processor shall cooperate with the Controller and take reasonable commercial steps to assist in the investigation, mitigation, and remediation of any Personal Data Breach. The Processor shall take immediate steps to contain and mitigate the effects of any Personal Data Breach and shall document all facts relating to the breach, its effects, and the remedial action taken.
120	10.4 The Processor shall not inform any third party of a Personal Data Breach without the Controller's prior written consent, unless required by Applicable Data Protection Law to make such disclosure. 28	16.1 The provisions of this Section 16 constitute a Business Associate Agreement between the Controller (as Covered Entity) and the Processor (as Business Associate) within the meaning of 45 C.F.R. § 164.504(e).
29	16.2 Permitted Uses and Disclosures. The Processor shall not use or disclose PHI other than as permitted or required by this DPA, or as required by law. The Processor shall use appropriate safeguards, including administrative, physical, and technical safeguards that reasonably and appropriately protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the electronic PHI that it creates, receives, maintains, or transmits on behalf of the Controller, in accordance with 45 C.F.R. Part 164, Subpart C. The Processor shall comply with the applicable requirements of 45 C.F.R. Part 164, Subpart C, with respect to electronic PHI.
31	16.4 Breach Reporting. The Processor shall report to the Controller any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this DPA of which it becomes aware, including breaches of unsecured PHI as required by 45 C.F.R. § 164.410. 35	16.8 Accounting of Disclosures. The Processor shall make available to the Controller the information required to provide an accounting of disclosures in accordance with 45 C.F.R. § 164.528. The Processor shall maintain records of disclosures of PHI and information related to such disclosures for a period of six (6) years from the date of the disclosure.
36	16.9 Access to Records. 90	The subject matter of the Processing is the provision of hosting and managed services for the StrattonCare telemedicine platform by the Processor on behalf of the Controller, in accordance with the Master Services Agreement dated March 3, 2025. 113	•  (b) Clinical records: diagnoses, prescriptions, laboratory results, imaging reports, clinical notes, treatment plans, referral records, allergy information;

121	•  Protected Health Information ("PHI") as defined under HIPAA and its implementing regulations.

127	The Processor shall implement and maintain the following technical and organizational security measures in connection with the Processing of Personal Data under this DPA:

143	•  4.2 Penetration testing shall be conducted at least annually by an independent third party. Results and remediation plans shall be made available to the Controller upon request.

155	•  8.1 The Processor shall maintain a documented incident response plan, tested at least annually.
156	•  8.2 The incident response plan shall include procedures for identification, containment, eradication, recovery, and lessons learned.
157	9. Logging and Monitoring
158	•  9.1 The Processor shall maintain comprehensive audit logs of all access to, and processing of, Personal Data.
159	•  9.2 Logs shall be protected against unauthorized modification and retained for a minimum period of twelve (12) months.
